title: Coherent terms of a finite-projective total tensor
statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let P and N be cochain complexes of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose P^n is zero outside a fixed integer interval [a,b], and for every n there are maps P^n to O_X^m and O_X^m to P^n whose composite on P^n is the identity, for some finite rank m. Suppose every term of N is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], without any boundedness assumption on N. Then every term of the signed direct-sum total complex Tot(P tensor N) [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is coherent.

source.place: perfect.tex, label lemma-tensor-perfect (0DJQ), displayed finite sum in its proof; coherent.tex, label lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian (01Y0)

proof.text: For a splitting F --ι--> G --π--> F with ι ≫ π = identity, define d = identity - π ≫ ι on G. The kernel of d is canonically isomorphic to F: its map to F is kernel.ι d ≫ π and the inverse is kernel.lift d ι. Check both identities using the splitting and kernel.condition. Kernel closure and isomorphism invariance from coherent_kernel_cokernel_sum prove that every retract of a coherent sheaf is coherent. This is the proved private helper coherent_retract.

Extend the Fin-indexed coherent finite-sum clause to an arbitrary finite index type using Finite.exists_equiv_fin and biproduct.whiskerEquiv. The proved private helper coherent_biproduct includes the empty index case. Identify free(ULift(Fin m)) tensor G with the biproduct of m copies of G, using biproduct.isoCoproduct, tensorRight.mapBiproduct and the left unitor. The tensorRight additive and finite-biproduct-preservation instances are the existing source implementation in WeilConjectures.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.MonoidalFree; no application of the bundled tensorClosed theorem is needed. This proves the private helper coherent_free_tensor. Tensor each given splitting of P^p with N^q, check the splitting by Functor.map_comp and map_id, and apply coherent_retract to get coherent summands.

Fix total degree i and let J be the pairs (p,q) with p+q=i and p in Finset.Icc a b. Projection onto p injects J into that finite interval; uniqueness of q follows by integer arithmetic. Let F(j)=P^p tensor N^q, which is coherent by the preceding step, and hence its finite biproduct is coherent. Define backMap from this biproduct to the total term using biproduct.desc and ιMapBifunctor. Define forwardMap from the total term to this biproduct using mapBifunctorDesc: a summand in the interval maps by its biproduct inclusion, and one outside maps by zero. The composite forwardMap ≫ backMap is the identity by mapBifunctor.hom_ext: inside the interval use ι_mapBifunctorDesc and biproduct.ι_desc; outside, hPbounds and Functor.map_isZero for tensorRight show the source is zero, so its outgoing maps agree. Thus the total term is a retract of the coherent finite biproduct and is coherent by coherent_retract. The same construction handles a>b, rank zero, empty schemes and unbounded N.

proof_origin.place: Finite-sum calculation in the proof of 0DJQ; coherent kernel and finite-sum closure from 01Y0/01BY. Lean assembly uses a retract of the surviving finite biproduct and the existing source tensorRight implementation.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteRetract_tensorComplex_coherent_terms
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (P N : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (a b : ℤ)
    (hPbounds : ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n))
    (hPfree : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ m : ℕ,
      ∃ (ι : P.X n ⟶ SheafOfModules.free
          (R := moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin m)))
        (π : SheafOfModules.free
          (R := moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) ⟶ P.X n),
        ι ≫ π = 𝟙 (P.X n))
    (hNcoherent : ∀ n : ℤ, RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (N.X n)) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace
        ((CochainComplex.mapBifunctor P N (curriedTensor _)).X i)
